pool.text: The Tuileries Garden was created for the Tuileries Palace.
The Luxembourg Garden was built for Marie de' Medici.
The Jardin des plantes was created as the first botanical garden.
The Royal Academy of Painting and Sculpture was established.
The Comédie-Française was founded as the oldest Paris theatre.
La Taverne Anglaise was opened by Antoine Beauvilliers in the Palais-Royal.
French police and gendarmes arrested thousands of Jews and confined them at the Vel d'Hiv.
American and French forces liberated the city from occupation during the war.
Le Lido music hall opened on the Champs-Élysées.
UNESCO established its headquarters in Paris.
Protest demonstrations by Algerians led to violent confrontations and multiple deaths.
Paul Delouvrier became head of the Paris region.
Protesting students occupied the Sorbonne and built barricades in the Latin Quarter.
The District de la région parisienne was reorganised into new departments.
The Périphérique expressway encircling the city was completed.
Charles de Gaulle Airport opened to commercial traffic.
The district of the Paris region was renamed Île-de-France.
The central river banks including major landmarks were classified as a World Heritage Site.
Bertrand Delanoë became the first socialist mayor of the capital.
A section of the highway along the Left Bank became an urban promenade.
